title: Quantitative bound on hyperbolic absolutely continuous invariant measures for one-dimensional maps
difficulty_reason: The count is obtained from a uniform positive basin-size bound proved using geometric times and bounded distortion, with the required positive-density and empirical-measure construction supplied in the author source. The proof of Proposition 4 then makes the reparametrization scale quantitative via the iterate-derivative norm and the choice of p. These source-specific obligations, including the full author chain below, remain part of the proof rather than an unexplained prerequisite. Proposition 3.1 is already present as 2537 and is not counted again.

readability.basis: Existing 35-page reader from batch-14872-14875-r004; physically inspected page 3 containing Proposition 4 and page 33 containing its complete proof. Full work remains accessible; original source and references retained.

dedup.scope: Current base master title searches for physical measure, absolutely continuous invariant measure, geometric time, Lyapunov, SRB measure and ACIP, and text searches combining Lyapunov exponent with basin or absolutely continuous with physical measure; exact source and named nearby entries compared. Titles alone are not the uniqueness basis.

compared.relation: Same paper Proposition 3.1 bounds the measure of strongly expanding points with sparse geometric times; candidate bounds the count of absolutely continuous invariant measures satisfying a basin-intersection condition. 2537 is an author proof dependency, not an alternate proof of the same proposition.

The retained lemma partsum estimates weighted partition sums on a hyperbolic uniformity block for a diffeomorphism, rather than bounding counts of one-dimensional absolutely continuous invariant measures.
The selected result concerns spectral-radius growth of finite-dimensional linear cocycles, not basin sizes or the number of invariant measures.
